title: Our AI trader's $5k paper account is up 21.5%. Here's the full curve.
author: Kamla_AI
selftext:
I'm part of the team building Kamla, an AI trader that reads market news and makes one trading decision per market day through Alpaca.

This is our $5,000 paper account: up 21.50% since funding as of Sept 26. The chart runs from June 10 to Sept 26, including that sharp dip before August.

How do you handle those stretches with your own systems? Do you pause at a fixed drawdown, or let the strategy keep running?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
paper is exactly where pausing on drawdown costs you something, because the drawdown is the data you're running the account to collect. I let mine run through it and write down what each rule did, then decide later whether the rule or the tape was at fault.

on the curve, the comparison I'd want next to it is the same 5k parked in SPY from June 10 to today. one decision a day through a green summer draws a nice line either way, and the gap between the two lines is the actual result.

replies.author: Kamla_AI
replies.body: Fair point on letting paper drawdowns play out. The faint dotted line is SPY. I checked June 10–Sept 27: Kamla +21.50%, SPY +4.72% excluding dividends. On $5k, that's roughly $6,075 vs $5,236. I should've made the comparison clearer.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: dividends aside, the comparison I'd still want is exposure-matched: how much of the time the account was actually in the market. a paper account sitting in cash half the time and still ahead of SPY is a different claim from one fully invested the whole way, and a better one if it holds.

replies.author: Kamla_AI
replies.body: I pulled the June 10–Sept 27 history. The account had market exposure for about 97% of regular trading hours, with roughly 68% of equity invested on average. Both are time-weighted estimates from account snapshots.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 97% of hours in and 68% invested makes it a mostly-invested claim, which is the harder one to beat, so good. the fair line under the curve is then 0.68 x SPY's return from June 10 plus cash on the rest, not SPY flat. if the account still clears that, the number in your title is doing real work rather than riding beta.

replies.author: Kamla_AI
replies.body: Using that 68/32 SPY/cash split, I get about 3.2% versus our 21.5%, assuming no cash interest. Our allocation varied, so that's a rough benchmark rather than an exact exposure match.
